metrics.label: Favorites per 1,000 views
metrics.help: How often readers who opened the story added it to their favorites. Dividing by views makes stories that have been read a lot comparable with stories that have been read a little.

metrics.label: Comments per 1,000 views
metrics.help: Public comments left on the story, per 1,000 views.

metrics.label: Ratings per 1,000 views
metrics.help: How many readers gave the story a star rating, per 1,000 views.

metrics.label: Reading-list adds per 1,000 views
metrics.more: are added to more reading lists per 1,000 views
metrics.less: are added to fewer reading lists per 1,000 views
metrics.help: How often readers saved the story to one of their reading lists, per 1,000 views.

metrics.label: Views per month
metrics.help: Total views divided by the number of months the story has been online. A simple way to compare old and new stories, since older stories have had longer to collect views.

metrics.label: Views
metrics.help: Total views shown on the story page when it was collected.

metrics.label: Favorites
metrics.help: Total number of readers who added the story to their favorites.

metrics.label: Ratings (number of)
metrics.help: How many readers gave the story a star rating.

metrics.label: Average rating
metrics.help: The average star rating (1 to 5) shown on the story page. Most stories score between 4 and 5, so small differences can matter.

topics.label: Narration
topics.blurb: First or third person, tense, talking to the reader
topics.syn: pov point of view person narrator tense voice

topics.label: Dialogue & characters
topics.syn: dialog speech talking conversation quotes characters names pronouns gender

topics.label: Sexual content
topics.blurb: How much, how early, how varied
topics.syn: explicit sex sexual smut erotic steamy spicy heat

topics.label: Emotion & relationships
topics.syn: feelings mood sentiment love romance relationship consent

topics.label: Pacing & setting
topics.blurb: What builds up, what peaks where, where it happens
topics.syn: pace build-up structure setting location place

topics.label: Word choice & style
topics.syn: writing style vocabulary readability grammar punctuation

topics.label: When published
topics.syn: date time when age old new

variables.label: Publication year
variables.description: Year the story was published.

variables.label: Publication month
variables.description: Month the story was published.

variables.label: Publication weekday
variables.description: Day of the week the story was published.

variables.label: Published on a weekend
variables.description: Whether the story was published on a Saturday or Sunday.

variables.label: Years online
variables.description: How long the story had been online when its numbers were recorded, in years.

variables.label: Pages on site
variables.description: Number of web pages the story is split into.

variables.label: Number of tags
variables.description: Number of tags the author attached.

variables.label: Author’s story count
variables.description: Number of stories the author had published (public profile count) when collected.
variables.caveat: Measured at collection time, not at publication time. Shown in bands (1, 2–5, 6–20, 21–50, 51–100, 101–200, 201+) so that authors stay anonymous.

variables.label: Word count
variables.description: Number of words in the story text (letters/digits, contractions count as one word). Author’s notes, headings and similar notes around the story are not counted.

variables.label: Sentence count
variables.description: Number of sentences.

variables.label: Paragraph count
variables.description: Number of non-empty story paragraphs (paratext excluded).

variables.label: Average sentence length
variables.description: Average number of words per sentence.

variables.label: Median sentence length
variables.description: Median number of words per sentence.

variables.label: Average paragraph length
variables.description: Average number of words per paragraph.

variables.label: Median paragraph length
variables.description: Median number of words per paragraph.

variables.label: One-sentence paragraphs
variables.description: Share of paragraphs that consist of a single sentence.

variables.label: Very long paragraphs (‘walls of text’)
variables.description: Share of paragraphs longer than 150 words.

variables.label: Scene breaks per 1,000 words
variables.description: Scene-break lines per 1,000 words.
variables.more: Stories with more scene breaks per 1,000 words

variables.label: Has an author’s note
variables.description: Whether the story opens or closes with an author’s or editor’s note, disclaimer, dedication, copyright line or words to readers, or has a paragraph labeled as an author’s note.
variables.caveat: Rule-based; misses notes that use no recognizable wording (about 1 in 3 in a hand check).

variables.label: Title length
variables.description: Number of characters in the title.

variables.label: Title word count
variables.description: Number of words in the title.

variables.label: Title marks a chapter/part
variables.description: Whether the title contains a chapter or part marker such as ‘Ch. 02’, ‘Pt. 3’ or ends with a number.
variables.yes_subject: Stories whose title marks a chapter or part

variables.label: Description length
variables.description: Number of characters in the author’s short description.

variables.label: Description word count
variables.description: Number of words in the description.

variables.label: Explicit title
variables.description: Whether the title contains a term from the sexual word lists.
variables.caveat: Not measured when there is no title.

variables.label: Explicit description
variables.description: Whether the description contains a term from the sexual word lists.
variables.caveat: Not measured when there is no description.

variables.label: Person of the description
variables.description: Grammatical person of the description: first (I, my, we), second (you), third (he, she, they), by which personal pronouns it uses most, or none.
variables.caveat: About two descriptions in three use no personal pronoun (‘none’).
variables.noun: the person used in the description

variables.label: Part of a series
variables.description: Whether the story belongs to a series (series link on the page, a series of 2+ parts, or a chapter marker in the title).

variables.label: Part number
variables.description: Which part of its series the story is (1 = first), from the series list or the title.

variables.label: Later part of a series
variables.description: Whether the story is part 2 or later of a series.

variables.label: Opens with speech
variables.description: Whether the first word of the story (after any author’s note or heading) is inside quotation marks.
variables.caveat: Stories written without quotation marks (chat logs, scripts) never count.

variables.label: Ends with speech
variables.description: Whether the last word of the story (before any closing note) is inside quotation marks.
variables.caveat: Stories written without quotation marks (chat logs, scripts) never count.

variables.label: Announces a continuation
variables.description: Whether the story ends by announcing more to come (‘to be continued’, ‘next chapter’, ‘part 3 coming soon’) in its last three paragraphs or its closing note.
variables.caveat: What the author announced, not whether a sequel exists; chapters of long works often leave it out.

variables.label: We / us / our
variables.description: First-person plural pronouns per 1,000 words.
variables.syn: pov point of view person narrator 1st person first person
variables.more: Stories that use ‘we / us / our’ more

variables.label: You / your
variables.description: Second-person pronouns per 1,000 words.
variables.syn: pov point of view person narrator 1st person first person

variables.label: I / me / my in narration
variables.description: First-person singular pronouns per 1,000 words of narration (outside quotation marks).
variables.noun: the use of ‘I / me / my’ in the narration
variables.syn: pov point of view person narrator 1st person first person
variables.more: Stories whose narration uses ‘I / me / my’ more

variables.label: We / us / our in narration
variables.description: First-person plural pronouns per 1,000 narration words (outside quotation marks).
variables.noun: the use of ‘we / us / our’ in the narration
variables.syn: pov point of view person narrator 1st person first person
variables.more: Stories whose narration uses ‘we / us / our’ more

variables.label: You / your in narration
variables.description: Second-person pronouns per 1,000 narration words.
variables.noun: the use of ‘you / your’ in the narration
variables.syn: pov point of view person narrator 1st person first person
variables.more: Stories whose narration uses ‘you / your’ more

variables.label: He / she / they in narration
variables.description: Third-person pronouns per 1,000 narration words.
variables.noun: the use of ‘he / she / they’ in the narration
variables.syn: pov point of view person narrator 1st person first person
variables.more: Stories whose narration uses ‘he / she / they’ more

variables.label: First-person share of pronouns
variables.description: In narration, first-person pronouns as a share of first- plus third-person pronouns.
variables.caveat: A word-counting rule, not a reading of the story; see How it works for how it was validated.
variables.syn: pov point of view person narrator 1st person first person
variables.more: Stories with a larger first-person share of pronouns

variables.label: Narrative perspective
variables.unit: first / first_plural / second / third / mixed / unknown
variables.description: Estimated from the pronouns in the narration, leaving dialogue out: plenty of I/me/my means first person; ‘we’ narration and ‘you’ narration have their own groups; very few I/me/my compared with he/she/they means third person; anything in between is mixed. Stories with under 200 words of narration are left out.
variables.caveat: A word-counting rule, not a reading of the story; see How it works for how it was validated.
variables.syn: pov point of view person narrator 1st person first person

variables.label: First-person narration
variables.description: Compares stories narrated in the first person (I, or we) with stories narrated in the third person. Second-person and mixed stories are left out here; “Narrative perspective” shows them all.
variables.caveat: A word-counting rule, not a reading of the story; see How it works for how it was validated.
variables.syn: pov point of view person narrator 1st person first person

variables.label: Present-tense share
variables.description: In narration, present-tense forms of ~70 common verbs as a share of present plus past forms.
variables.caveat: Not measured if fewer than 20 such verbs occur. A rule-based estimate.
variables.noun: the present-tense share of the narration
variables.more: Stories told more in the present tense

variables.label: Narration tense
variables.description: Present tense if at least 60% of the narration’s verbs are in the present tense, past tense if 40% or fewer, mixed in between.

variables.label: Present-tense narration
variables.description: Compares stories narrated mostly in the present tense with stories narrated mostly in the past tense. Mixed stories are left out here; “Narration tense” shows them all.

variables.label: Talking to the reader
variables.description: Narration that speaks to the reader (‘trust me’, ‘believe me’, ‘let me tell you’, ‘dear reader’, ‘as you can imagine’) per 1,000 narration words.
variables.caveat: Not measured under 200 narration words. One story’s value rests on only a few instances and is noisy; summaries of groups, as shown here, are steadier.
variables.noun: how often the narration talks to the reader
variables.more: Stories that talk to the reader more

variables.label: Dialogue share
variables.description: Share of words inside quotation marks.
variables.caveat: Depends on consistent quotation marks; stories using none score 0 even if they contain speech.

variables.label: Dialogue segments per 1,000 words
variables.description: Number of separate quoted passages per 1,000 words.
variables.more: Stories with more dialogue segments per 1,000 words

variables.label: Average speech length
variables.description: Average number of words per quoted passage.

variables.label: Questions asked in dialogue
variables.description: Share of all question marks that occur inside quotation marks.
variables.more: Stories with more questions in their dialogue

variables.label: Exclamations in dialogue
variables.description: Share of all exclamation marks that occur inside quotation marks.
variables.more: Stories with more exclamations in their dialogue

variables.label: Paragraphs with dialogue
variables.description: Share of paragraphs that contain at least one quoted passage.
variables.more: Stories with more paragraphs of dialogue

variables.label: Has dialogue
variables.description: Whether the story has any quoted speech.

variables.label: Untagged speech lines
variables.description: Share of dialogue paragraphs made only of quoted speech, with no narration and no ‘she said’.
variables.caveat: Not measured with fewer than 5 dialogue paragraphs.
variables.more: Stories with more untagged speech lines

variables.label: Adverbs in speech tags
variables.description: Share of speech tags (a speech verb within four words of a quotation) with an -ly adverb next to the verb (‘she said softly’, ‘he whispered hoarsely’).
variables.caveat: Not measured with fewer than 5 speech tags.
variables.more: Stories with more adverbs in speech tags

variables.label: Dialogue/narration alternation
variables.description: How often the story switches between dialogue and narration paragraphs, compared with a random order: below 1 means dialogue comes in blocks (scenes), above 1 means dialogue and narration alternate.
variables.caveat: Not measured unless there are at least 5 dialogue and 5 narration paragraphs. One story’s value rests on only a few instances and is noisy; summaries of groups, as shown here, are steadier.
variables.noun: how often dialogue and narration alternate
variables.more: Stories that switch more between dialogue and narration

variables.label: Recurring names
variables.description: Number of distinct capitalized names that appear at least 3 times mid-sentence (mostly characters, sometimes places).
variables.caveat: A rule-based estimate: first names and surnames count separately. Common titles, places, nationalities, organizations and brands are left out, as is a word that mostly follows ‘the’ or ‘in’, but rarer ones can still count (about 9 in 10 detected names were characters in a hand check); names that only ever start a sentence are missed.
variables.more: Stories with more recurring named characters

variables.label: Name mentions per 1,000 words
variables.description: Mentions of those recurring names per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Lower in short stories, where fewer names reach the three mentions needed to count.
variables.more: Stories that mention names more often

variables.label: Focus on one main name
variables.description: Share of all name mentions taken by the most-mentioned name.
variables.more: Stories focused more on one main name

variables.label: He / him / his
variables.description: Masculine pronouns per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Pronouns describe the characters on the page, not the author; first-person narrators’ gender is invisible to this measure.
variables.more: Stories that use ‘he / him / his’ more

variables.label: She / her / hers
variables.description: Feminine pronouns per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Pronouns describe the characters on the page, not the author; first-person narrators’ gender is invisible to this measure.
variables.more: Stories that use ‘she / her / hers’ more

variables.label: They / them / their
variables.description: They/them/their pronouns per 1,000 words (plural or singular).
variables.caveat: Pronouns describe the characters on the page, not the author; first-person narrators’ gender is invisible to this measure.
variables.more: Stories that use ‘they / them / their’ more

variables.label: Feminine share of he/she pronouns
variables.description: Feminine pronouns as a share of feminine plus masculine pronouns.
variables.caveat: Pronouns describe the characters on the page, not the author; first-person narrators’ gender is invisible to this measure.
variables.noun: the feminine share of he/she pronouns
variables.more: Stories with a larger share of she/her among he/she pronouns

variables.label: Pronoun composition
variables.description: Mostly she/her if at least 65% of the he/she pronouns are feminine, mostly he/him if 35% or fewer, and “few he/she” when there are fewer than 5 such pronouns per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Pronouns describe the characters on the page, not the author; first-person narrators’ gender is invisible to this measure.

variables.label: Ellipses
variables.description: Ellipses (‘…’ or ‘...’) per 1,000 words. Lines made only of dots are scene breaks, not ellipses.

variables.label: Dashes
variables.description: Dashes per 1,000 words: em dashes (‘—’), runs of hyphens (‘--’), and a hyphen or en dash with a space on each side used as a dash (‘she paused - then left’). Hyphens inside words are not dashes.

variables.label: Semicolons
variables.description: Semicolons per 1,000 words.

variables.label: Colons
variables.description: Colons per 1,000 words.

variables.label: Commas
variables.description: Commas per 1,000 words.

variables.label: Quotation marks
variables.description: Double quotation marks per 1,000 words.

variables.label: Parentheses
variables.description: Opening parentheses per 1,000 words.

variables.label: Repeated punctuation (!!, ?!)
variables.description: Runs of two or more ! or ? marks (e.g. ‘!!’, ‘?!’) per 1,000 words.

variables.label: Question sentences
variables.description: Share of sentences that end with a question mark.
variables.more: Stories with a larger share of questions

variables.label: Exclamation sentences
variables.description: Share of sentences that end with an exclamation mark.
variables.more: Stories with a larger share of exclamations

variables.label: Questions per 1,000 words
variables.description: Sentences ending in a question mark per 1,000 words.
variables.more: Stories with more questions per 1,000 words

variables.label: Exclamations per 1,000 words
variables.description: Sentences ending in an exclamation mark per 1,000 words.
variables.more: Stories with more exclamations per 1,000 words

variables.label: Average word length
variables.description: Average number of letters per word.

variables.label: Syllables per word
variables.description: Average estimated syllables per word.
variables.caveat: Syllables are estimated with a spelling rule (~85–90% exact per word).
variables.more: Stories with more syllables per word

variables.label: Long (3+ syllable) words
variables.description: Share of words with three or more syllables.
variables.more: Stories with more long (3+ syllable) words

variables.label: Reading ease (Flesch)
variables.description: How easy the text is to read: higher scores mean shorter sentences and shorter words. Calculated with the Flesch Reading Ease formula (206.835 − 1.015 × words per sentence − 84.6 × syllables per word).
variables.caveat: Dialogue-heavy text has short sentences and scores as easy.

variables.label: Reading difficulty (grade)
variables.description: Average of the Flesch–Kincaid, ARI and Coleman–Liau grade levels: a single ‘estimated school grade’.

variables.label: Commas per sentence
variables.description: Average number of commas per sentence (a rough sign of longer, multi-part sentences).
variables.more: Stories with more commas per sentence

variables.label: Subordinate clauses per sentence
variables.description: Words that usually start a dependent clause (because, although, which, when…) per sentence.

variables.label: Long sentences (>30 words)
variables.description: Share of sentences longer than 30 words.

variables.label: Short sentences (≤5 words)
variables.description: Share of sentences of five words or fewer.

variables.label: Sentence-length variety
variables.description: Standard deviation of sentence length: how much sentence lengths vary.
variables.more: Stories with more varied sentence lengths

variables.label: Unique words
variables.description: Number of different words used.
variables.caveat: Grows with story length; compare stories of similar length or use the moving-average measure.

variables.label: Word variety (type–token ratio)
variables.description: Different words divided by all words: how varied the vocabulary is (the type–token ratio).
variables.caveat: Strongly depends on length (longer texts always score lower); prefer “Vocabulary variety (moving average)”.
variables.more: Stories with a higher type–token ratio (more varied words)

variables.label: Vocabulary variety (moving average)
variables.description: The share of different words in each 500-word stretch, averaged over the story, so that long and short stories can be compared (a moving-average type–token ratio).
variables.caveat: Needs at least 500 words (window size); blank for shorter stories.

variables.label: Everyday vocabulary
variables.description: How common the story’s words are on average, on a scale where about 7 is as common as ‘the’ and 3 is rare (the Zipf scale of a standard English word-frequency list).

variables.label: Rare words
variables.description: Share of words that are rare in English (fewer than about one in a million words).

variables.label: Unrecognized words
variables.description: Share of words not in the English frequency list: names, invented words, typos or non-English words.
variables.caveat: Not a spelling-error rate: names and slang count too.

variables.label: Long words (7+ letters)
variables.description: Share of words with seven or more letters.

variables.label: Focus on a few words
variables.description: Within each 500-word window, the share of content words (not function words) taken by the 10 most frequent ones, averaged.
variables.caveat: Needs at least 500 words (window size); blank for shorter stories.
variables.more: Stories that lean more on a few favorite words

variables.label: Repeated word pairs
variables.description: Within each 500-word window, the share of two-word sequences that occur more than once (ignoring pairs of function words), averaged.
variables.caveat: Needs at least 500 words (window size); blank for shorter stories.
variables.more: Stories with more repeated word pairs

variables.label: Repeated three-word phrases
variables.description: As above for three-word sequences.
variables.caveat: Needs at least 500 words (window size); blank for shorter stories.
variables.more: Stories with more repeated three-word phrases

variables.label: Overlap between neighboring sentences
variables.description: Average share of content words that consecutive sentences have in common (Jaccard overlap).
variables.more: Stories whose neighboring sentences overlap more

variables.label: Sentences starting the same way
variables.description: Share of sentences that start with the same word as the sentence before (‘She… She… She…’).
variables.more: Stories with more sentences that start the same way

variables.label: Doubled words
variables.description: Words immediately repeated (‘yes, yes’, ‘oh oh’) per 1,000 words.

variables.label: Repeated five-word phrases
variables.description: Extra occurrences of any five-word sequence that appears more than once within the same 1,000-word stretch, per 1,000 words.
variables.more: Stories with more repeated five-word phrases

variables.label: Profanity
variables.description: Swear words per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Overlaps with the sexual-action list for ‘fuck’.
variables.syn: swearing cursing swear words curse words bad language

variables.label: ALL-CAPS words
variables.description: Words written entirely in capitals (2+ letters, common acronyms excluded) per 1,000 words.

variables.label: -ly adverbs
variables.description: Words ending in -ly (excluding common non-adverbs like ‘only’, ‘family’, ‘lovely’) per 1,000 words.

variables.label: Plain ‘said’ in dialogue tags
variables.description: ‘said’/‘says’ as a share of all speech verbs (said, asked, whispered, moaned…).
variables.caveat: Not measured when fewer than 5 speech verbs occur.
variables.more: Stories that use plain ‘said’ more in speech tags

variables.label: Physical action verbs
variables.description: Verbs of physical movement (grab, pull, turn, reach…) per 1,000 words.
variables.more: Stories with more physical action verbs

variables.label: Descriptive words
variables.description: Descriptive adjectives and material words (beautiful, tall, slender, satin…) per 1,000 words.

variables.label: Italics
variables.description: Italicized passages per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Italics are counted over the whole page body, author’s notes included.

variables.label: Stretched words
variables.description: Words with a letter repeated three or more times (‘ohhh’, ‘yesss’, ‘mmmm’) per 1,000 words.

variables.label: Writing slips
variables.description: All the writing-mechanics slips below, plus doubled small words (‘the the’), per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Counts slips a spell-checker or proofreader would catch; dialogue written in dialect can count too.

variables.label: Sexual language
variables.description: Sexual terms per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: A keyword count from editable word lists; it does not measure how explicit a story feels to a reader.

variables.label: Anatomical terms
variables.description: Explicit or clinical words for sexual body parts per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: A keyword count from editable word lists; it does not measure how explicit a story feels to a reader.

variables.label: Sexual-action terms
variables.description: Words and phrases for sexual acts per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: A keyword count from editable word lists; it does not measure how explicit a story feels to a reader.

variables.label: General sexual words
variables.description: General sexual words (sex, naked, erotic, toys, lingerie) per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: A keyword count from editable word lists; it does not measure how explicit a story feels to a reader.
variables.more: Stories with more general sexual words

variables.label: Sentences with sexual language
variables.description: Share of sentences containing at least one sexual term.
variables.caveat: A keyword count from editable word lists; it does not measure how explicit a story feels to a reader.
variables.noun: the share of sentences with sexual language
variables.more: Stories in which more sentences contain sexual language

variables.label: Words before first explicit term
variables.description: Number of words before the first sexual term (‘slow burn’).
variables.caveat: Not measured if the story has none.
variables.noun: words before the first explicit term
variables.more: Stories that take longer to reach explicit language

variables.label: Variety of sexual vocabulary
variables.description: Number of different sexual-language words used.
variables.more: Stories with more varied sexual vocabulary

variables.label: Sex scenes
variables.description: Number of separate sex-dense stretches: 200-word windows with at least 6 sexual terms (30 per 1,000 words, about 1.75 times the median story’s rate), slid in 50-word steps; overlapping windows count as one scene.
variables.caveat: Not measured under 400 words. Depends on story length like every count: compare with “Sex scenes per 10,000 words”. A dense stretch is usually sexual activity, but can be an essay-like passage or a conversation about sex (about 1 in 4 in a hand check).

variables.label: Sex scenes per 10,000 words
variables.description: Sex scenes (see “Sex scenes”) per 10,000 words: how often the story returns to a sex scene.
variables.caveat: Not measured under 400 words.
variables.more: Stories with more sex scenes for their length

variables.label: Where the first sex scene starts
variables.description: Start of the first sex-dense stretch as a fraction of the story: the build-up before the first real scene, which a passing early mention does not trigger.
variables.caveat: Not measured if there is no such stretch or under 400 words.
variables.noun: where the first sex scene starts
variables.more: Stories whose first sex scene starts later

variables.label: Emotional words (all)
variables.description: Words from any emotion list per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Keyword counts: negation (‘not happy’) and sarcasm are not understood.

variables.label: Positive emotion
variables.description: Positive-emotion and affection words per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Keyword counts: negation (‘not happy’) and sarcasm are not understood.

variables.label: Negative emotion
variables.description: Negative-emotion, anxiety, anger, sadness, shame and jealousy words per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Keyword counts: negation (‘not happy’) and sarcasm are not understood.

variables.label: Affection & love
variables.description: Words of love and fondness per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Keyword counts: negation (‘not happy’) and sarcasm are not understood.
variables.more: Stories with more affection and love

variables.label: Anxiety & fear
variables.description: Words of fear, worry and nervousness per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Keyword counts: negation (‘not happy’) and sarcasm are not understood. One story’s value rests on only a few instances and is noisy; summaries of groups, as shown here, are steadier.
variables.more: Stories with more anxiety and fear

variables.label: Anger
variables.description: Words of anger and irritation per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Keyword counts: negation (‘not happy’) and sarcasm are not understood. One story’s value rests on only a few instances and is noisy; summaries of groups, as shown here, are steadier.

variables.label: Sadness
variables.description: Words of sadness, crying and loneliness per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Keyword counts: negation (‘not happy’) and sarcasm are not understood.

variables.label: Excitement & arousal
variables.description: Words of excitement, desire and arousal per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Keyword counts: negation (‘not happy’) and sarcasm are not understood.
variables.more: Stories with more excitement and arousal

variables.label: Shame & embarrassment
variables.description: Words of shame, embarrassment, guilt and shyness per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Keyword counts: negation (‘not happy’) and sarcasm are not understood.
variables.more: Stories with more shame and embarrassment

variables.label: Jealousy & envy
variables.description: Words of jealousy and envy per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Keyword counts: negation (‘not happy’) and sarcasm are not understood. One story’s value rests on only a few instances and is noisy; summaries of groups, as shown here, are steadier.
variables.more: Stories with more jealousy and envy

variables.label: Emotional tone
variables.description: (positive − negative) ÷ (positive + negative) emotion words.
variables.caveat: Keyword counts: negation (‘not happy’) and sarcasm are not understood.
variables.more: Stories with a more positive emotional tone

variables.label: Humor and laughter
variables.description: Laughing and joking (laugh, giggle, chuckle, joke, funny, ‘lol’) per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: Keyword counts: negation (‘not happy’) and sarcasm are not understood.
variables.more: Stories with more humor and laughter

variables.label: Thinking verbs
variables.description: Mental-state verbs (think, know, realize, wonder…) per 1,000 words.

variables.label: Perception verbs

variables.label: Passive constructions

variables.caveat: A rule-based estimate (about 9 in 10 counted matches were passives in a hand check): common participles that describe a state or feeling (‘was dressed in’, ‘was accustomed to’, ‘was fascinated by’) are left out; rarer ones (‘was unrequited’) still count.

variables.label: Spoken commands
variables.description: Quoted passages containing a command, i.e. a sentence that starts with a command verb, possibly after ‘please’, ‘now’ or a name (‘Come here.’, ‘Kneel.’, ‘Sarah, don’t stop.’), per 1,000 words.
variables.caveat: A rule-based estimate: question sentences, ‘Do you…’, ‘Look, …’ / ‘Listen, …’ as fillers and ‘fuck’ as an expletive are left out; commands whose verb is not on the list are missed.

variables.label: Commands among speech

variables.label: Consent and check-in language

variables.caveat: Counts language, not depicted consent: a check-in can be ignored in the story, and refusals are not counted. Essays that discuss consent score high.
